summary: Taj Mahal is a classic Knizia design where players bid across multiple simultaneous auctions each round using a hand of cards, competing to control regions and collect commodities that convert to influence points. It's tense and cutthroat, with every auction affecting your standing relative to your neighbors.
praised: High player interaction and tough decisions
Elegant design that rewards reading opponents
criticised: Can feel mean or kingmaking in some groups
Auction mechanism takes a play or two to click

interaction.kind: bidding against each other for regional control and palace favors
interaction.detail: Each round is a hidden-then-revealed bidding war for control of regions and the resources/favors in them, so your commodity and card gains are frequently won or lost directly at an opponent's expense. Building palaces requires currying favor from the same small pool of nobles everyone else is chasing, keeping most of the fight centered on shared, contested resources rather than a private board.
interaction.said: Knizia's auction games in this style are frequently called 'vicious' and 'cutthroat' — players talk about the palace/region bidding wars and how a single card played against you can flip control of a region.

scoring.how_you_win: Across 12 regions, win card auctions to build an escalating chain of palaces and collect commodities; after the final region, whoever has the most combined palace and commodity-majority points wins.
